escena: SCENE (cinematic, Hollywood blockbuster still with real depth of field, a vast dark studio at night): ONE monumental frameless LED wall, about four meters wide, stands at an oblique angle behind and to the LEFT of a Latin American creative director in her mid thirties, dark curly shoulder-length hair, wearing the Efeonce hoodie exactly as in its reference. The wall shows one bold campaign image of a fictitious brand with an unmistakable visual signature: a single sweeping vivid orange (#FF6500) brushstroke shape cutting across a deep navy night photograph, grainy and photographic. In the lower right corner of the wall, where the logo would sit, a wide strip of matte black gaffer tape covers it completely, slightly wrinkled, one corner lifting. The brand is still instantly recognisable. She stands slightly RIGHT of center in the lower part of the frame, framed from the waist up, her body turned toward the wall and her head almost frontal, looking straight into the lens with a knowing, amused half-smile, holding the half-used roll of black tape against her chest. Far behind, out of focus in the haze, EXACTLY TWO smaller screens repeat the same brushstroke signature in other formats (a tall vertical film frame and a phone), each also with tape over its logo corner. LIGHT: the LED wall is the only key light: hard, from the left, warm orange on the left side of her face, hand and hoodie, the right side of her face in soft shadow with the nose shadow legible; NO fill light. A cool azure (#0375DB) rim light from behind outlines her hair and right shoulder. Thin haze catches the glow of the wall. REALISTIC ADULT PROPORTIONS: camera about two meters away at chest height, 85mm at f/2, nothing foreshortened, she does not lean toward the lens. Fine dust, real sensor grain, genuine depth of field. The TOP 30% of the frame is calm, deep dark studio space with only faint haze, no screen, no light, no objects; the LED wall stays below 34% of the frame height. Enormous contrast, deep navy blacks, punchy color. No readable text, no letters, no logos of any brand anywhere.

lecho.objeto: the near-black matte edge of a long work table close to the lens across the whole bottom of the frame, completely out of focus, outside every light and every reflection

texto.muro: calm, deep dark studio space with only faint haze
